about: Every voiced line of the chapter's ink: who speaks it, the exact words shown on the page ("text"), and what the voice is given ("say": the same words with eleven_v3 audio tags). tools/lines.mjs --check voices.json proves "text" matches the ink; tools/directions.py writes this file. Each line has "takes" takes, media/vo/<id>-1.mp3 and so on, and one more if its id is in "secondTake"; the page plays one at random.

evening.speaker: quaile
evening.text: That's the day gone. Vicarage, Sam.
evening.say: [drily] That's the day gone. Vicarage, Sam.

hub-0.speaker: quaile
hub-0.text: The coroner sits on Friday. Five people to see and time for four. Where first?
hub-0.say: [drily] The coroner sits on Friday. Five people to see and time for four. Where first?

hub-3.speaker: quaile
hub-3.text: One more, then the vicarage. Dr Achebe says she's made a spreadsheet.
hub-3.say: [drily] One more, then the vicarage. Dr Achebe says she's made a spreadsheet.

morning.speaker: narrator
morning.text: Wednesday. You sleep for four hours, and wake to your phone.
morning.say: [dry, unhurried] Wednesday. You sleep for four hours, and wake to your phone.

morning-drone.speaker: narrator
morning-drone.text: A video from Toby Pike, sent at six. He was flying a drone over the schoolhouse on Tuesday night, and thought you might like it.
morning-drone.say: [dry, unhurried] A video from Toby Pike, sent at six. He was flying a drone over the schoolhouse on Tuesday night, and thought you might like it.

morning-rows.speaker: narrator
morning-rows.text: An email from Dilys, forwarded from Perth, with the subject line Not your best.
morning-rows.say: [dry, unhurried] An email from Dilys, forwarded from Perth, with the subject line Not your best.

p1-open.speaker: narrator
p1-open.text: St Aldhelm's, a Tuesday in October, twenty past seven. Three months after the Marrow Show, the interim vicar has talked you into learning to ring the bells.
p1-open.say: [wry] St Aldhelm's, a Tuesday in October, twenty past seven. [short pause] Three months after the Marrow Show, the interim vicar has talked you into learning to ring the bells.

p10-open.speaker: narrator
p10-open.text: Sunday, the harvest service. Marrows on the font, and on the wall the Jubilee board under a purple cloth, to be blessed after the notices. Jeremy Cole is in the front pew, in a suit.
p10-open.say: [dry, unhurried] Sunday, the harvest service. Marrows on the font, and on the wall the Jubilee board under a purple cloth, to be blessed after the notices. Jeremy Cole is in the front pew, in a suit.

p10a-1.speaker: achebe
p10a-1.text: Notices. The flower rota is in the porch. The roof fund stands at four thousand two hundred pounds.
p10a-1.say: [calm, amused, precise] Notices. The flower rota is in the porch. The roof fund stands at four thousand two hundred pounds.

p10a-2.speaker: achebe
p10a-2.text: Hugh Daventry's funeral will be here on Thursday at eleven. Margaret is doing the flowers.
p10a-2.say: [calm, amused, precise] Hugh Daventry's funeral will be here on Thursday at eleven. Margaret is doing the flowers.

p10b-1.speaker: narrator
p10b-1.text: Jeremy Cole sits in the front pew with his hymn book shut. He has not looked at the cloth.
p10b-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Jeremy Cole sits in the front pew with his hymn book shut. He has not looked at the cloth.

p10c-1.speaker: narrator
p10c-1.text: You lift the corner of the purple cloth. The gold on the date is still tacky. The letters have little feet now.
p10c-1.say: [dry, unhurried] You lift the corner of the purple cloth. The gold on the date is still tacky. The letters have little feet now.

p10c-2.speaker: sam
p10c-2.text: It's the board from his barn. He swapped them.
p10c-2.say: [measured] It's the board from his barn. He swapped them.

p10c-3.speaker: sam
p10c-3.text: That's not the board I saw on Tuesday.
p10c-3.say: [measured] That's not the board I saw on Tuesday.

p10c-4.speaker: narrator
p10c-4.text: Achebe stops the notices and looks at you over her glasses.
p10c-4.say: [dry, unhurried] Achebe stops the notices and looks at you over her glasses.

p10e-brush.speaker: sam
p10e-brush.text: So you lettered a new one in your barn, and swapped it this week.
p10e-brush.say: [measured] So you lettered a new one in your barn, and swapped it this week.

p10e-hunch.speaker: jeremy
p10e-hunch.text: I rang every blow, Sergeant. Ask anyone in the band.
p10e-hunch.say: [smooth, warm] I rang every blow, Sergeant. Ask anyone in the band.

p10e-named.speaker: sam
p10e-named.text: On Tuesday the band moved up one, and you rang the four. When the lights went, the four stopped dead for forty seconds.
p10e-named.say: [measured] On Tuesday the band moved up one, and you rang the four. When the lights went, the four stopped dead for forty seconds.

p10e-proof.speaker: sam
p10e-proof.text: Hugh died holding the corner of a proof. Peal board, a correction. You have the rest of that page.
p10e-proof.say: [measured] Hugh died holding the corner of a proof. Peal board, a correction. You have the rest of that page.

p10e-rows.speaker: sam
p10e-rows.text: When the lights went, one bell stopped dead for forty seconds.
p10e-rows.say: [measured] When the lights went, one bell stopped dead for forty seconds.

p10e-typeface.speaker: sam
p10e-typeface.text: The board you sold this church for nine thousand pounds is lettered in Gill Sans. Gill Sans was released in nineteen twenty-eight.
p10e-typeface.say: [measured] The board you sold this church for nine thousand pounds is lettered in Gill Sans. Gill Sans was released in nineteen twenty-eight.

p10f-achebe.speaker: achebe
p10f-achebe.text: Eleven per cent, Sergeant. I did say.
p10f-achebe.say: [calm, amused, precise] Eleven per cent, Sergeant. I did say.

p10f-dilys.speaker: dilys
p10f-dilys.text: I was on the two, love, and talking to you the whole time. You heard me.
p10f-dilys.say: [loud, cheerful] I was on the two, love, and talking to you the whole time. You heard me.

p10f-win.speaker: win
p10f-win.text: I had the three, Sergeant. I kept it going in the dark. Ask Glenys.
p10f-win.say: [loud, indignant] I had the three, Sergeant. I kept it going in the dark. Ask Glenys.

p10g-1.speaker: quaile
p10g-1.text: Sit down, Sam. Mr Cole, Hugh was going to print a correction about your board. You went down the stair in the dark to get it back.
p10g-1.say: [drily] Sit down, Sam. Mr Cole, Hugh was going to print a correction about your board. You went down the stair in the dark to get it back.

p10g-3.speaker: narrator
p10g-3.text: Dr Achebe blesses the board. Jeremy Cole holds the cloth for her.
p10g-3.say: [dry, unhurried] Dr Achebe blesses the board. Jeremy Cole holds the cloth for her.

p10h-1.speaker: jeremy
p10h-1.text: He was going to print it in the November magazine. Every house in the village gets one.
p10h-1.say: [low, fast] He was going to print it in the November magazine. Every house in the village gets one.

p10h-2.speaker: jeremy
p10h-2.text: I went down to ask him for the page. He held on to it and stepped back, and there isn't a step there.
p10h-2.say: [quiet, flat] I went down to ask him for the page. He held on to it and stepped back, and there isn't a step there.

p10h-3.speaker: quaile
p10h-3.text: And then you went back up and rang.
p10h-3.say: [quiet] And then you went back up and rang.

p10h-4.speaker: jeremy
p10h-4.text: I didn't know what else to do.
p10h-4.say: [very quiet] I didn't know what else to do.

p10i-1.speaker: narrator
p10i-1.text: After the service the band rings for the harvest. Five ropes. Win back on the four.
p10i-1.say: [dry, unhurried] After the service the band rings for the harvest. Five ropes. Win back on the four.

p10i-2.speaker: narrator
p10i-2.text: Dr Achebe rings the five, and gets it right twice.
p10i-2.say: [dry, unhurried] Dr Achebe rings the five, and gets it right twice.

p10i-3.speaker: narrator
p10i-3.text: Jeremy Cole rings the five, every blow.
p10i-3.say: [dry, unhurried] Jeremy Cole rings the five, every blow.

p10i-4.speaker: narrator
p10i-4.text: The ropes come to rest. Win puts her hand flat on the wall, then looks up at the tenor's rope, still tied to its hook.
p10i-4.say: [quiet] The ropes come to rest. Win puts her hand flat on the wall, then looks up at the tenor's rope, still tied to its hook.

p1a-1.speaker: narrator
p1a-1.text: Rooks go round the spire. Up in the ringing chamber, a light is on.
p1a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Rooks go round the spire. Up in the ringing chamber, a light is on.

p1a-2.speaker: narrator
p1a-2.text: The bicycle rack by the lychgate is empty. Hugh Daventry rings the treble, edits the parish magazine and sets the Wednesday quiz at the Plough. He usually leaves his bicycle there by a quarter past.
p1a-2.say: [dry] The bicycle rack by the lychgate is empty. Hugh Daventry rings the treble, edits the parish magazine and sets the Wednesday quiz at the Plough. He usually leaves his bicycle there by a quarter past.

p1b-1.speaker: achebe
p1b-1.text: Sergeant Adeyemi. You came. I told Margaret forty per cent.
p1b-1.say: [pleased] Sergeant Adeyemi. You came. I told Margaret forty per cent.

p1b-3.speaker: achebe
p1b-3.text: She said you'd come if you'd said you would.
p1b-3.say: [amused] She said you'd come if you'd said you would.

p1b-4.speaker: narrator
p1b-4.text: The Reverend Dr Ruth Achebe has been the interim vicar since August. Before she was ordained she priced pension risk for an insurer in Croydon.
p1b-4.say: [dry, unhurried] The Reverend Dr Ruth Achebe has been the interim vicar since August. Before she was ordained she priced pension risk for an insurer in Croydon.

p1b-again.speaker: achebe
p1b-again.say: [calm, amused, precise] Win's waiting for you, Sergeant.

p1c-1.speaker: win
p1c-1.text: You're the policeman. I'm Win. Tower captain.
p1c-1.say: [too loud, brisk] You're the policeman. I'm Win. Tower captain.

p1c-2.speaker: narrator
p1c-2.text: She is seventy-eight. She speaks a little too loudly, and she watches your mouth while you answer. A reporter's notebook and a pencil hang on a string round her neck.
p1c-2.say: [dry, unhurried] She is seventy-eight. She speaks a little too loudly, and she watches your mouth while you answer. A reporter's notebook and a pencil hang on a string round her neck.

p1c-3.speaker: win
p1c-3.text: You sit on the bench with your feet in, and you don't touch a rope. A bell can lift a grown man to the ceiling.
p1c-3.say: [loud, stern] You sit on the bench with your feet in, and you don't touch a rope. A bell can lift a grown man to the ceiling.

p1d-1.speaker: narrator
p1d-1.text: On the back of a napkin from the Plough she writes out the first thing every ringer learns.
p1d-1.say: [dry, unhurried] On the back of a napkin from the Plough she writes out the first thing every ringer learns.

p1d-2.speaker: win
p1d-2.text: Plain hunt. Five bells. In one row the pairs swap: one with two, three with four. In the next, two with three, four with five. Then the first again.
p1d-2.say: [loud, brisk] Plain hunt. Five bells. In one row the pairs swap: one with two, three with four. In the next, two with three, four with five. Then the first again.

p1d-3.speaker: win
p1d-3.text: Ten rows and you're back in rounds. Hugh rings the treble. If he isn't here by half past, we ring on five.
p1d-3.say: [loud, brisk] Ten rows and you're back in rounds. Hugh rings the treble. If he isn't here by half past, we ring on five.

p1d-5.speaker: win
p1d-5.text: Six bells. On five, the tenor stays down.
p1d-5.say: [loud, brisk] Six bells. On five, the tenor stays down.

p2-open.speaker: narrator
p2-open.text: The ringing chamber, up fourteen stone steps: six ropes with striped woollen grips, a bench, a tea tray and a blackboard. Five ringers, and one rope tied up out of reach.
p2-open.say: [dry, unhurried] The ringing chamber, up fourteen stone steps: six ropes with striped woollen grips, a bench, a tea tray and a blackboard. Five ringers, and one rope tied up out of reach.

p2a-1.speaker: narrator
p2a-1.text: Margaret Pike pours tea from a flask on the windowsill. She puts out two cups, looks at the second one, and puts it back in the basket.
p2a-1.say: [quiet] Margaret Pike pours tea from a flask on the windowsill. She puts out two cups, looks at the second one, [short pause] and puts it back in the basket.

p2a-2.speaker: margaret
p2a-2.text: Sergeant. Milk's in the jam jar.
p2a-2.say: [quiet, precise] Sergeant. Milk's in the jam jar.

p2a-cold.speaker: narrator
p2a-cold.text: She hands you a cup without looking at you.
p2a-cold.say: [dry, unhurried] She hands you a cup without looking at you.

p2b-1.speaker: narrator
p2b-1.text: On the blackboard, in Hugh's square capitals: Tuesday. One, Hugh. Two, Margaret. Three, Dilys. Four, Win. Five, Jeremy. Six, Ruth.
p2b-1.say: [dry, unhurried] On the blackboard, in Hugh's square capitals: Tuesday. One, Hugh. Two, Margaret. Three, Dilys. Four, Win. Five, Jeremy. Six, Ruth.

p2b-2.speaker: dilys
p2b-2.text: Hugh's not come, so we all move up one. Margaret, you're on the treble. Ruth, you sit this one out.
p2b-2.say: [loud, cheerful] Hugh's not come, so we all move up one. Margaret, you're on the treble. Ruth, you sit this one out.

p2b-3.speaker: dilys
p2b-3.text: Don't change the board, love. Hugh likes to rub it out himself.
p2b-3.say: [loud, warning] Don't change the board, love. Hugh likes to rub it out himself.

p2b-cold.speaker: dilys
p2b-cold.text: Hugh's not come. Win'll sort us out.
p2b-cold.say: [loud, cheerful] Hugh's not come. Win'll sort us out.

p2c-1.speaker: win
p2c-1.text: Look to. Treble's going. She's gone.
p2c-1.say: [loud, ringing call] Look to. Treble's going. [short pause] She's gone.

p2c-2.speaker: narrator
p2c-2.text: The bells start overhead, loud enough to feel through the bench. Five people stand in a circle, each watching somebody else's rope.
p2c-2.say: [dry, unhurried] The bells start overhead, loud enough to feel through the bench. Five people stand in a circle, each watching somebody else's rope.

p2c-3.speaker: narrator
p2c-3.text: Jeremy Cole, the antiques dealer, stands nearest the door, under the light switch. At five past eight, between two pieces, he reads his phone and puts it away.
p2c-3.say: [dry, unhurried] Jeremy Cole, the antiques dealer, stands nearest the door, under the light switch. At five past eight, between two pieces, he reads his phone and puts it away.

p2c-again.speaker: narrator
p2c-again.text: The ropes go up and down. Win's lips move as she counts.
p2c-again.say: [dry, unhurried] The ropes go up and down. Win's lips move as she counts.

p2d-1.speaker: narrator
p2d-1.text: At a quarter past eight, the lights go out.
p2d-1.say: [low] At a quarter past eight, the lights go out.

p2d-2.speaker: narrator
p2d-2.text: The ringing goes on in the dark, and goes wrong: a bell is missing from the pattern, or two are. Below you, through the floor, there is a thud and a short metal rattle.
p2d-2.say: [low, tense] The ringing goes on in the dark, and goes wrong: a bell is missing from the pattern, or two are. Below you, through the floor, there is a thud and a short metal rattle.

p2d-3.speaker: narrator
p2d-3.text: Forty seconds by your watch, and the lights come back. Everybody is where they were.
p2d-3.say: [dry, unhurried] Forty seconds by your watch, and the lights come back. Everybody is where they were.

p2d-4.speaker: jeremy
p2d-4.text: That switch does it every winter. You have to hold it up.
p2d-4.say: [breezy, a little out of breath] That switch does it every winter. You have to hold it up.

p2d-5.speaker: narrator
p2d-5.text: Win calls Stand, and the bells stop. Dr Achebe goes down the stair first, to put the kettle on.
p2d-5.say: [dry, unhurried] Win calls Stand, and the bells stop. Dr Achebe goes down the stair first, to put the kettle on.

p3-again.speaker: narrator
p3-again.text: The vestry, at the foot of the stair.
p3-again.say: [dry, unhurried] The vestry, at the foot of the stair.

p3-open.speaker: narrator
p3-open.text: Hugh Daventry is at the foot of the tower stair, where it comes down into the vestry. Dr Achebe is kneeling beside him. She looks up and shakes her head.
p3-open.say: [quiet, grave] Hugh Daventry is at the foot of the tower stair, where it comes down into the vestry. Dr Achebe is kneeling beside him. [short pause] She looks up and shakes her head.

p3a-1.speaker: narrator
p3a-1.text: His bicycle clips are still on. His torch lies on the bottom step, still lit.
p3a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] His bicycle clips are still on. His torch lies on the bottom step, still lit.

p3a-2.speaker: narrator
p3a-2.text: The stair is stone, narrow, and turns to the left. Fourteen steps up to the ringing chamber door.
p3a-2.say: [dry, unhurried] The stair is stone, narrow, and turns to the left. Fourteen steps up to the ringing chamber door.

p3a-3.speaker: achebe
p3a-3.text: He texted the band at five past eight. On my way up. Something to say about the board. H.
p3a-3.say: [calm, amused, precise] He texted the band at five past eight. On my way up. Something to say about the board. H.

p3a-4.speaker: achebe
p3a-4.text: I came down for the kettle and he was here. I haven't moved him.
p3a-4.say: [quiet, steady] I came down for the kettle and he was here. I haven't moved him.

p3b-1.speaker: narrator
p3b-1.text: His right hand is closed on the corner of a page, torn off. Printed on it: Peal board, a corre. And at the bottom, H.D.
p3b-1.say: [dry, unhurried] His right hand is closed on the corner of a page, torn off. Printed on it: Peal board, a corre. And at the bottom, H.D.

p3b-2.speaker: sam
p3b-2.text: A proof. For the parish magazine.
p3b-2.say: [measured] A proof. For the parish magazine.

p3b-3.speaker: sam
p3b-3.text: Somebody has the rest of that page.
p3b-3.say: [measured] Somebody has the rest of that page.

p3c-1.speaker: narrator
p3c-1.text: Quaile arrives eleven minutes later, in a raincoat over pyjamas.
p3c-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Quaile arrives eleven minutes later, in a raincoat over pyjamas.

p3c-2.speaker: quaile
p3c-2.text: I was in the bath, Sam. Tell me it's an accident.
p3c-2.say: [weary] I was in the bath, Sam. [short pause] Tell me it's an accident.

p3c-4.speaker: quaile
p3c-4.text: Then why did you ring me and not just an ambulance?
p3c-4.say: [sharp] Then why did you ring me and not just an ambulance?

p3c-6.speaker: quaile
p3c-6.text: Old man, stone stair, lights out. The coroner will say he fell, and the coroner sits on Friday. The band are cold and want their beds. You can ask them one thing tonight.
p3c-6.say: [drily] Old man, stone stair, lights out. The coroner will say he fell, and the coroner sits on Friday. The band are cold and want their beds. You can ask them one thing tonight.

p3c-again.speaker: quaile
p3c-again.text: One question for the band, Sam, then they go home.
p3c-again.say: [drily] One question for the band, Sam, then they go home.

p3d-1.speaker: narrator
p3d-1.text: The band waits in the vestry in their coats: Win, Dilys, Margaret, Jeremy. Nobody sits down.
p3d-1.say: [dry, unhurried] The band waits in the vestry in their coats: Win, Dilys, Margaret, Jeremy. Nobody sits down.

p3d-again.speaker: narrator
p3d-again.text: The band waits in their coats. They have answered one question, and would like to go home.
p3d-again.say: [dry, unhurried] The band waits in their coats. They have answered one question, and would like to go home.

p3e-1.speaker: dilys
p3e-1.text: In the dark? Nobody could have found the door, love.
p3e-1.say: [loud, cheerful] In the dark? Nobody could have found the door, love.

p3e-2.speaker: jeremy
p3e-2.text: We rang straight through, Sergeant. Ask Win.
p3e-2.say: [smooth, warm] We rang straight through, Sergeant. Ask Win.

p3f-1.speaker: dilys
p3f-1.text: I record every practice for my sister Glenys. She's in Perth. Rang here for thirty years, before her knees went.
p3f-1.say: [loud, cheerful] I record every practice for my sister Glenys. She's in Perth. Rang here for thirty years, before her knees went.

p3f-2.speaker: dilys
p3f-2.text: She listens over her breakfast and marks us out of ten.
p3f-2.say: [loud, cheerful] She listens over her breakfast and marks us out of ten.

p3f-3.speaker: dilys
p3f-3.text: I'll send it to her tonight. You'll have her marks by morning.
p3f-3.say: [loud, cheerful] I'll send it to her tonight. You'll have her marks by morning.

p3f-cold.speaker: dilys
p3f-cold.text: You can have it when I've decided whether I like you yet. Ask me tomorrow.
p3f-cold.say: [loud, cheerful] You can have it when I've decided whether I like you yet. Ask me tomorrow.

p3g-1.speaker: margaret
p3g-1.text: We moved up one, because Hugh hadn't come. I had the treble. It was my first time on the treble.
p3g-1.say: [quiet, precise] We moved up one, because Hugh hadn't come. I had the treble. It was my first time on the treble.

p3g-2.speaker: margaret
p3g-2.text: Gerald never let me ring. He said it was bad for the hands.
p3g-2.say: [quiet, precise] Gerald never let me ring. He said it was bad for the hands.

p3g-cold.speaker: margaret
p3g-cold.text: Ask Win, Sergeant. She'll tell you. Loudly.
p3g-cold.say: [quiet, precise] Ask Win, Sergeant. She'll tell you. Loudly.

p3g-cold2.speaker: narrator
p3g-cold2.text: Win is already putting her coat on.
p3g-cold2.say: [dry, unhurried] Win is already putting her coat on.

p4-open.speaker: narrator
p4-open.text: Win Haskett's cottage, the last in Church Row. A brass bell for a knocker, which she cannot hear, and beside it a button that makes a lamp flash inside.
p4-open.say: [dry, unhurried] Win Haskett's cottage, the last in Church Row. A brass bell for a knocker, which she cannot hear, and beside it a button that makes a lamp flash inside.

p4a-1.speaker: narrator
p4a-1.text: A card in the window, in capitals: Shoes off. This means you.
p4a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] A card in the window, in capitals: Shoes off. This means you.

p4b-1.speaker: win
p4b-1.text: Come in. Tea's stewed. Sit there, not there.
p4b-1.say: [loud, brisk] Come in. Tea's stewed. Sit there, not there.

p4b-2.speaker: narrator
p4b-2.text: Quaile takes out her hearing aid and puts it down by the teapot.
p4b-2.say: [dry, unhurried] Quaile takes out her hearing aid and puts it down by the teapot.

p4b-4.speaker: narrator
p4b-4.text: Win tears one page off the notepad for your questions and pushes it across the table.
p4b-4.say: [dry, unhurried] Win tears one page off the notepad for your questions and pushes it across the table.

p4b-again.speaker: narrator
p4b-again.text: Win taps the notepad and looks at the clock.
p4b-again.say: [dry, unhurried] Win taps the notepad and looks at the clock.

p4c-1.speaker: narrator
p4c-1.text: She writes a large 4, underlines it twice, and adds: Forty-one years.
p4c-1.say: [dry, unhurried] She writes a large 4, underlines it twice, and adds: Forty-one years.

p4c-3.speaker: narrator
p4c-3.text: Underneath, Quaile writes: Is the tea always like this? Win writes: Yes.
p4c-3.say: [dry, unhurried] Underneath, Quaile writes: Is the tea always like this? Win writes: Yes.

p4d-1.speaker: narrator
p4d-1.text: Win writes for a long time.
p4d-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Win writes for a long time.

p4d-2.speaker: narrator
p4d-2.text: Hugh never came. Moved up one. Plain hunt on five, tenor down. I had the 3. Lights out at 8.14. Could not see the ropes, so I kept mine going and counted.
p4d-2.say: [dry, unhurried] Hugh never came. Moved up one. Plain hunt on five, tenor down. I had the 3. Lights out at 8.14. Could not see the ropes, so I kept mine going and counted.

p4d-3.speaker: narrator
p4d-3.text: Underneath, underlined: Somebody dropped out. Ask Dilys for Glenys's tape.
p4d-3.say: [dry, unhurried] Underneath, underlined: Somebody dropped out. Ask Dilys for Glenys's tape.

p4e-1.speaker: narrator
p4e-1.text: Her phone, on the mantelpiece by the clock. The band's group, Tuesday, five past eight. Hugh: On my way up. Something to say about the board. H.
p4e-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Her phone, on the mantelpiece by the clock. The band's group, Tuesday, five past eight. Hugh: On my way up. Something to say about the board. H.

p4e-2.speaker: win
p4e-2.text: I read it when I got home. Phones stay in coats in my tower.
p4e-2.say: [loud, pointed] I read it when I got home. Phones stay in coats in my tower.

p5-again.speaker: narrator
p5-again.text: The barn on the Cirencester road.
p5-again.say: [dry, unhurried] The barn on the Cirencester road.

p5-open.speaker: narrator
p5-open.text: Cole Antiques: a stone barn on the Cirencester road, full of other people's chairs. Over the door, a sign: Restored with Sympathy.
p5-open.say: [dry, unhurried] Cole Antiques: a stone barn on the Cirencester road, full of other people's chairs. Over the door, a sign: Restored with Sympathy.

p5a-1.speaker: narrator
p5a-1.text: Every chair has a price on a brown luggage label. The cheapest is four hundred pounds.
p5a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Every chair has a price on a brown luggage label. The cheapest is four hundred pounds.

p5a-2.speaker: narrator
p5a-2.text: A radio on the workbench is playing the shipping forecast.
p5a-2.say: [dry, unhurried] A radio on the workbench is playing the shipping forecast.

p5b-1.speaker: jeremy
p5b-1.text: Sergeant. Inspector. I heard this morning. Hugh and I didn't always agree, but he was good company on quiz nights.
p5b-1.say: [smooth, sorrowful] Sergeant. Inspector. I heard this morning. Hugh and I didn't always agree, but he was good company on quiz nights.

p5b-3.speaker: narrator
p5b-3.text: He wipes his hands on a cloth that has gold on it. He has time for one question before the dresser.
p5b-3.say: [dry, unhurried] He wipes his hands on a cloth that has gold on it. He has time for one question before the dresser.

p5b-again.speaker: jeremy
p5b-again.text: Anything else, Sergeant? I have a dresser coming at two.
p5b-again.say: [smooth, warm] Anything else, Sergeant? I have a dresser coming at two.

p5c-1.speaker: jeremy
p5c-1.text: On the five, ringing, every blow, start to finish. Five is my bell. Ask anyone in the band.
p5c-1.say: [smooth, confident] On the five, ringing, every blow, start to finish. Five is my bell. Ask anyone in the band.

p5c-2.speaker: jeremy
p5c-2.text: When the lights went I kept going. You do. Rope's in your hands.
p5c-2.say: [smooth, warm] When the lights went I kept going. You do. Rope's in your hands.

p5d-1.speaker: jeremy
p5d-1.text: The Jubilee board? Found it in a barn at Bibury, under a tarpaulin. The tower's own, taken down in the sixties. Restored with sympathy.
p5d-1.say: [smooth, warm] The Jubilee board? Found it in a barn at Bibury, under a tarpaulin. The tower's own, taken down in the sixties. Restored with sympathy.

p5d-2.speaker: jeremy
p5d-2.text: The parish paid nine thousand pounds, out of the roof fund. A pub in Bath offered me twelve.
p5d-2.say: [smooth, warm] The parish paid nine thousand pounds, out of the roof fund. A pub in Bath offered me twelve.

p5d-3.speaker: quaile
p5d-3.text: The roof fund has had a hard year.
p5d-3.say: [drily] The roof fund has had a hard year.

p5e-1.speaker: narrator
p5e-1.text: On a trestle at the back, a board under a dust sheet, and a sign-writer's brush across a pot of gold size. The gold is still wet.
p5e-1.say: [dry, unhurried] On a trestle at the back, a board under a dust sheet, and a sign-writer's brush across a pot of gold size. The gold is still wet.

p5e-2.speaker: narrator
p5e-2.text: Under the sheet: a peal board, half lettered. Jubilee, eighteen ninety-seven. These letters have small feet on them, like the lettering on old shop fronts.
p5e-2.say: [dry, unhurried] Under the sheet: a peal board, half lettered. Jubilee, eighteen ninety-seven. These letters have small feet on them, like the lettering on old shop fronts.

p5e-3.speaker: jeremy
p5e-3.text: A commission. Another church. I'm not at liberty.
p5e-3.say: [smooth, quickly] A commission. Another church. [short pause] I'm not at liberty.

p5f-1.speaker: narrator
p5f-1.text: His van says Cole Antiques in gold, in plain round letters with no feet at all.
p5f-1.say: [dry, unhurried] His van says Cole Antiques in gold, in plain round letters with no feet at all.

p6-open.speaker: narrator
p6-open.text: The Plough. The quiz goes ahead: Hugh set the questions on Sunday, and the landlord reads them out from Hugh's sheet. Six teams and a fire.
p6-open.say: [dry, unhurried] The Plough. The quiz goes ahead: Hugh set the questions on Sunday, and the landlord reads them out from Hugh's sheet. Six teams and a fire.

p6a-1.speaker: narrator
p6a-1.text: The fire has been lit since four. The dog in front of it has not moved since five.
p6a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] The fire has been lit since four. The dog in front of it has not moved since five.

p6b-1.speaker: landlord
p6b-1.text: Round two. Question seven. In what year did Monotype release the typeface Gill Sans?
p6b-1.say: [into a microphone, cheerful] Round two. Question seven. [short pause] In what year did Monotype release the typeface Gill Sans?

p6b-2.speaker: narrator
p6b-2.text: At the bar, the landlord shows you Hugh's answer sheet. Against question seven, in pencil: Nineteen twenty-eight. And under it, smaller: Then look up in the tower.
p6b-2.say: [dry, unhurried] At the bar, the landlord shows you Hugh's answer sheet. Against question seven, in pencil: Nineteen twenty-eight. And under it, smaller: Then look up in the tower.

p6b-3.speaker: quaile
p6b-3.text: He was going to ask the whole village. Then tell them the answer in print.
p6b-3.say: [quiet, thoughtful] He was going to ask the whole village. Then tell them the answer in print.

p6c-1.speaker: narrator
p6c-1.text: Behind the bar, a photograph of Hugh at last year's quiz, in a bow tie, with the microphone.
p6c-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Behind the bar, a photograph of Hugh at last year's quiz, in a bow tie, with the microphone.

p6c-2.speaker: landlord
p6c-2.text: He never let the same team win twice running. Said it was bad for the village.
p6c-2.say: [warm, gruff] He never let the same team win twice running. Said it was bad for the village.

p6d-1.speaker: dilys
p6d-1.text: Glenys rang me at six this morning to ask if she's evidence.
p6d-1.say: [loud, cheerful] Glenys rang me at six this morning to ask if she's evidence.

p6d-2.speaker: dilys
p6d-2.text: I was cross with you last night. I'm less cross now. Here.
p6d-2.say: [loud, cheerful] I was cross with you last night. I'm less cross now. Here.

p6d-3.speaker: narrator
p6d-3.text: She forwards you an email from Perth. The subject line is Not your best.
p6d-3.say: [dry, unhurried] She forwards you an email from Perth. The subject line is Not your best.

p6d-4.speaker: dilys
p6d-4.text: My sister's got a recording of Tuesday, if anyone had thought to ask. Nobody did. Here.
p6d-4.say: [loud, cheerful] My sister's got a recording of Tuesday, if anyone had thought to ask. Nobody did. Here.

p6d-again.speaker: dilys
p6d-again.text: Shush, love, it's the music round.
p6d-again.say: [loud, cheerful] Shush, love, it's the music round.

p7-open.speaker: narrator
p7-open.text: The old schoolhouse, closed since nineteen ninety-one, with a For Sale board. Toby Pike is flying a drone over it for the brochure.
p7-open.say: [dry, unhurried] The old schoolhouse, closed since nineteen ninety-one, with a For Sale board. Toby Pike is flying a drone over it for the brochure.

p7a-1.speaker: narrator
p7a-1.text: One swing left in the playground. The chains have been painted so many times they no longer clink.
p7a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] One swing left in the playground. The chains have been painted so many times they no longer clink.

p7b-1.speaker: toby
p7b-1.text: Sergeant! Come to buy a schoolhouse? Four bedrooms, original features, a bell nobody's allowed to ring.
p7b-1.say: [bright, salesman] Sergeant! Come to buy a schoolhouse? Four bedrooms, original features, a bell nobody's allowed to ring.

p7b-again.speaker: toby
p7b-again.say: [breezy, quick] Still here, Sergeant. Still selling.

p7b-cold.speaker: toby
p7b-cold.text: The sergeant who took my phone off me. I'm working.
p7b-cold.say: [breezy, quick] The sergeant who took my phone off me. I'm working.

p7b-warm.speaker: toby
p7b-warm.text: Did you get the video? I sent it at six. I don't sleep, I'm selling a school.
p7b-warm.say: [breezy, quick] Did you get the video? I sent it at six. I don't sleep, I'm selling a school.

p7c-1.speaker: toby
p7c-1.text: Oh. Right. Well. I was going to send you something anyway. Probably.
p7c-1.say: [breezy, quick] Oh. Right. Well. I was going to send you something anyway. Probably.

p7d-1.speaker: narrator
p7d-1.text: On his controller, Tuesday night, the church from the air, for the brochure's Village Life page.
p7d-1.say: [dry, unhurried] On his controller, Tuesday night, the church from the air, for the brochure's Village Life page.

p7d-2.speaker: narrator
p7d-2.text: Eight thirteen: a man wheels a bicycle through the lychgate. Eight fourteen: the ringing chamber window goes dark. Eight fifteen: it lights again. Nobody comes out of the church door until twenty past.
p7d-2.say: [dry, unhurried] Eight thirteen: a man wheels a bicycle through the lychgate. Eight fourteen: the ringing chamber window goes dark. Eight fifteen: it lights again. Nobody comes out of the church door until twenty past.

p7d-3.speaker: sam
p7d-3.text: So whoever it was never left the building.
p7d-3.say: [measured] So whoever it was never left the building.

p7d-4.speaker: toby
p7d-4.text: Can I still use the bit before eight?
p7d-4.say: [hopeful] Can I still use the bit before eight?

p7e-1.speaker: narrator
p7e-1.text: Tall church windows, a bell turret with no bell in it, and a board by the gate: Pike and Lowe, For Sale. Above the roof a drone hangs in the wind, filming.
p7e-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Tall church windows, a bell turret with no bell in it, and a board by the gate: Pike and Lowe, For Sale. Above the roof a drone hangs in the wind, filming.

p8-again.speaker: narrator
p8-again.say: [dry, unhurried] The ringing chamber, by daylight.

p8-open.speaker: narrator
p8-open.text: The ringing chamber by daylight. Dr Achebe is waiting with a magnifying glass from the vestry, and on the wall, the Jubilee board.
p8-open.say: [dry, unhurried] The ringing chamber by daylight. Dr Achebe is waiting with a magnifying glass from the vestry, and on the wall, the Jubilee board.

p8a-1.speaker: narrator
p8a-1.text: Black, with gold letters. Saint Aldhelm's. On the Diamond Jubilee of Her Majesty Queen Victoria, the twenty-second of June, eighteen ninety-seven, a peal of five thousand and forty changes. Six names.
p8a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Black, with gold letters. Saint Aldhelm's. On the Diamond Jubilee of Her Majesty Queen Victoria, the twenty-second of June, eighteen ninety-seven, a peal of five thousand and forty changes. Six names.

p8a-2.speaker: achebe
p8a-2.text: The parish bought it in March. Mr Cole found it in a barn. Hugh unveiled it. Hugh was not happy about something, and wouldn't say what.
p8a-2.say: [calm, amused, precise] The parish bought it in March. Mr Cole found it in a barn. Hugh unveiled it. Hugh was not happy about something, and wouldn't say what.

p8b-1.speaker: narrator
p8b-1.text: Under the glass the letters are clean and round. The R kicks its leg out straight. The small g has two loops, like spectacles.
p8b-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Under the glass the letters are clean and round. The R kicks its leg out straight. The small g has two loops, like spectacles.

p8b-2.speaker: quaile
p8b-2.text: My father had a railway timetable in those letters. He kept it in the downstairs toilet.
p8b-2.say: [fond, dry] My father had a railway timetable in those letters. He kept it in the downstairs toilet.

p8b-3.speaker: sam
p8b-3.text: Gill Sans. Nineteen twenty-eight. On a board from eighteen ninety-seven.
p8b-3.say: [measured] Gill Sans. Nineteen twenty-eight. On a board from eighteen ninety-seven.

p8b-5.speaker: achebe
p8b-5.text: Mr Cole told us he had regilded them.
p8b-5.say: [mild] Mr Cole told us he had regilded them.

p8c-1.speaker: achebe
p8c-1.text: On base rates, Inspector, it is usually the person who found him. That's me. I'd put myself at eleven per cent.
p8c-1.say: [calm, amused] On base rates, Inspector, it is usually the person who found him. That's me. [short pause] I'd put myself at eleven per cent.

p8c-3.speaker: achebe
p8c-3.text: They were all in the dark with me. I can't give odds on people I couldn't see.
p8c-3.say: [calm] They were all in the dark with me. I can't give odds on people I couldn't see.

p8c-again.speaker: achebe
p8c-again.text: Anything else up here, Sergeant? I have a funeral to plan.
p8c-again.say: [calm, amused, precise] Anything else up here, Sergeant? I have a funeral to plan.

p8d-1.speaker: achebe
p8d-1.text: You, Sergeant? You'll still be here at Christmas. Margaret has asked you to Sunday lunch, and you haven't said no.
p8d-1.say: [calm, amused, precise] You, Sergeant? You'll still be here at Christmas. Margaret has asked you to Sunday lunch, and you haven't said no.

p8d-3.speaker: achebe
p8d-3.text: She told me. She's bought a second chair.
p8d-3.say: [amused] She told me. She's bought a second chair.

p8d-cold.speaker: achebe
p8d-cold.text: You, Sergeant? You'll still be here at Christmas. You keep turning up to things you were only asked to once.
p8d-cold.say: [calm, amused, precise] You, Sergeant? You'll still be here at Christmas. You keep turning up to things you were only asked to once.

p8e-1.speaker: narrator
p8e-1.text: Dust in the light from the louvres. The ropes are tied up for the week, all but the treble.
p8e-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Dust in the light from the louvres. The ropes are tied up for the week, all but the treble.

p8e-2.speaker: narrator
p8e-2.text: The treble rope hangs free, and holding it, as if waiting to be told Look to, is a scarecrow in a navy mac and brown city shoes.
p8e-2.say: [dry, unhurried] The treble rope hangs free, and holding it, as if waiting to be told Look to, is a scarecrow in a navy mac and brown city shoes.

p8e-3.speaker: achebe
p8e-3.text: It was here when I unlocked this morning. I thought one of the band had brought it up.
p8e-3.say: [mild] It was here when I unlocked this morning. I thought one of the band had brought it up.

p9-open.speaker: narrator
p9-open.text: The vicarage kitchen, eleven at night. Dr Achebe has a spreadsheet open and the kettle on. Quaile has her shoes off.
p9-open.say: [dry, unhurried] The vicarage kitchen, eleven at night. Dr Achebe has a spreadsheet open and the kettle on. Quaile has her shoes off.

p9a-1.speaker: narrator
p9a-1.text: On the table: Win's napkin from the Plough, three mugs, and a plate of biscuits that Quaile is counting.
p9a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] On the table: Win's napkin from the Plough, three mugs, and a plate of biscuits that Quaile is counting.

p9b-1.speaker: narrator
p9b-1.text: Through the window, the tower against the rain. Somebody has left the light on in the ringing chamber.
p9b-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Through the window, the tower against the rain. Somebody has left the light on in the ringing chamber.

p9c-1.speaker: achebe
p9c-1.text: From Glenys in Perth. Dear Dilys. Not your best. You were going nicely on five till fourteen minutes past, then somebody says lights, and one bell stops dead for forty seconds.
p9c-1.say: [calm, amused, precise] From Glenys in Perth. Dear Dilys. Not your best. You were going nicely on five till fourteen minutes past, then somebody says lights, and one bell stops dead for forty seconds.

p9c-2.speaker: achebe
p9c-2.text: I can only hear four, so I've numbered them by note, highest first, as I hear them. Here's three rows.
p9c-2.say: [calm, amused, precise] I can only hear four, so I've numbered them by note, highest first, as I hear them. Here's three rows.

p9c-3.speaker: achebe
p9c-3.text: Then it comes back late and clumsy, like somebody out of breath. Win stood you at sixteen minutes past. Four out of ten. Love, G.
p9c-3.say: [calm, amused, precise] Then it comes back late and clumsy, like somebody out of breath. Win stood you at sixteen minutes past. Four out of ten. Love, G.

p9c-4.speaker: achebe
p9c-4.text: She can't tell which bell it was. She only hears the notes. But we have Win's napkin.
p9c-4.say: [calm, amused, precise] She can't tell which bell it was. She only hears the notes. But we have Win's napkin.

p9c-again.speaker: narrator
p9c-again.text: Glenys's three rows, on the screen: 2 4 1 3. 4 2 3 1. 4 3 2 1.
p9c-again.say: [dry, unhurried] Glenys's three rows, on the screen: 2 4 1 3. 4 2 3 1. 4 3 2 1.

p9c-none.speaker: narrator
p9c-none.text: Dr Achebe's spreadsheet has six columns headed One to Six, and nothing in them yet.
p9c-none.say: [dry, unhurried] Dr Achebe's spreadsheet has six columns headed One to Six, and nothing in them yet.

p9d-1.speaker: achebe
p9d-1.text: Take the one out, and that first row would sound 3 1 4 2. Glenys heard 2 4 1 3.
p9d-1.say: [calm, amused, precise] Take the one out, and that first row would sound 3 1 4 2. Glenys heard 2 4 1 3.

p9d-2.speaker: achebe
p9d-2.text: Take the two out, and that first row would sound 3 4 1 2. Glenys heard 2 4 1 3.
p9d-2.say: [calm, amused, precise] Take the two out, and that first row would sound 3 4 1 2. Glenys heard 2 4 1 3.

p9d-3.speaker: achebe
p9d-3.text: Take the three out, and that first row would sound 3 2 4 1. Glenys heard 2 4 1 3.
p9d-3.say: [calm, amused, precise] Take the three out, and that first row would sound 3 2 4 1. Glenys heard 2 4 1 3.

p9d-4.speaker: achebe
p9d-4.text: Take the four out. 4 2 5 1 3 becomes 2 5 1 3, and by note that's 2 4 1 3. Then 4 2 3 1. Then 4 3 2 1. Every row.
p9d-4.say: [quick, pleased] Take the four out. 4 2 5 1 3 becomes 2 5 1 3, and by note that's 2 4 1 3. Then 4 2 3 1. Then 4 3 2 1. [short pause] Every row.

p9d-5.speaker: achebe
p9d-5.text: Take the five out, and that first row would sound 4 2 1 3. Close. Glenys heard 2 4 1 3.
p9d-5.say: [calm, amused, precise] Take the five out, and that first row would sound 4 2 1 3. Close. Glenys heard 2 4 1 3.

p9d-6.speaker: sam
p9d-6.text: The four stopped for forty seconds, in the dark, and came back out of breath.
p9d-6.say: [measured] The four stopped for forty seconds, in the dark, and came back out of breath.

p9e-1.speaker: achebe
p9e-1.text: Don't ask me who had it. I was on a rope for the fourth time in my life. I couldn't have told you which one was mine.
p9e-1.say: [calm, amused, precise] Don't ask me who had it. I was on a rope for the fourth time in my life. I couldn't have told you which one was mine.

p9e-again.speaker: sam
p9e-again.text: Who had the four on Tuesday?
p9e-again.say: [measured] Who had the four on Tuesday?

p9f-1.speaker: sam
p9f-1.text: The board says Win. Forty-one years on the four. But not on Tuesday. Hugh never came, so they all moved up one. Win had the three.
p9f-1.say: [measured] The board says Win. Forty-one years on the four. But not on Tuesday. Hugh never came, so they all moved up one. Win had the three.

p9f-2.speaker: sam
p9f-2.text: The blackboard says Win. Four, Win.
p9f-2.say: [measured] The blackboard says Win. Four, Win.

p9f-3.speaker: quaile
p9f-3.text: That's who usually stands there, Sam. Is it who stood there on Tuesday?
p9f-3.say: [drily] That's who usually stands there, Sam. Is it who stood there on Tuesday?

p9g-1.speaker: sam
p9g-1.text: Hugh never came, so they all moved up one. Jeremy's bell is the five. On Tuesday he rang the four, next to the door and the light switch.
p9g-1.say: [measured] Hugh never came, so they all moved up one. Jeremy's bell is the five. On Tuesday he rang the four, next to the door and the light switch.

p9g-2.speaker: sam
p9g-2.text: And he told us he was on the five, every blow.
p9g-2.say: [measured] And he told us he was on the five, every blow.

p9g-5.speaker: quaile
p9g-5.text: The board says Jeremy rings the five, Sam. You'd want more than where he stood.
p9g-5.say: [drily] The board says Jeremy rings the five, Sam. You'd want more than where he stood.

p9h-1.speaker: sam
p9h-1.text: Dilys rings the three, and on Tuesday she moved up to the two. She was talking to me through most of it.
p9h-1.say: [measured] Dilys rings the three, and on Tuesday she moved up to the two. She was talking to me through most of it.

p9h-2.speaker: sam
p9h-2.text: Margaret had the treble. Her first time on it. Glenys would have heard the treble go.
p9h-2.say: [measured] Margaret had the treble. Her first time on it. Glenys would have heard the treble go.

p9i-board.speaker: quaile
p9i-board.text: Hugh wanted to say something about the board. Has anyone looked at it properly?
p9i-board.say: [drily] Hugh wanted to say something about the board. Has anyone looked at it properly?

p9i-good.speaker: quaile
p9i-good.text: I think you know. I'd like you to say it on Sunday, in front of the whole parish.
p9i-good.say: [drily] I think you know. I'd like you to say it on Sunday, in front of the whole parish.

p9i-rows.speaker: quaile
p9i-rows.text: Dilys records every practice. Has anyone asked her for Tuesday's?
p9i-rows.say: [drily] Dilys records every practice. Has anyone asked her for Tuesday's?

p9i-swap.speaker: quaile
p9i-swap.text: Hugh didn't come. So who was on which rope?
p9i-swap.say: [drily] Hugh didn't come. So who was on which rope?

p9i-warm.speaker: quaile
p9i-warm.text: You've learnt to ask me things, Sam. All right.
p9i-warm.say: [drily] You've learnt to ask me things, Sam. All right.

p9n-brush.speaker: narrator
p9n-brush.text: In Jeremy's barn, a second Jubilee board, half lettered, the gold still wet.
p9n-brush.say: [dry, unhurried] In Jeremy's barn, a second Jubilee board, half lettered, the gold still wet.

p9n-dark.speaker: narrator
p9n-dark.text: The drone: the chamber dark from eight fourteen to eight fifteen. Nobody left the church.
p9n-dark.say: [dry, unhurried] The drone: the chamber dark from eight fourteen to eight fifteen. Nobody left the church.

p9n-empty.speaker: narrator
p9n-empty.text: Your notebook has the date in it, and the words plain hunt.
p9n-empty.say: [dry, unhurried] Your notebook has the date in it, and the words plain hunt.

p9n-lie.speaker: narrator
p9n-lie.text: Jeremy says he rang the five, every blow.
p9n-lie.say: [dry, unhurried] Jeremy says he rang the five, every blow.

p9n-lie-b.speaker: narrator
p9n-lie-b.text: Jeremy says he rang the five, every blow, which is what the blackboard says.
p9n-lie-b.say: [dry, unhurried] Jeremy says he rang the five, every blow, which is what the blackboard says.

p9n-named.speaker: narrator
p9n-named.text: The silent bell was the four, and on Tuesday the four was Jeremy.
p9n-named.say: [dry, unhurried] The silent bell was the four, and on Tuesday the four was Jeremy.

p9n-proof.speaker: narrator
p9n-proof.text: In his hand, the corner of a proof: Peal board, a corre. The rest of the page is gone.
p9n-proof.say: [dry, unhurried] In his hand, the corner of a proof: Peal board, a corre. The rest of the page is gone.

p9n-quiz.speaker: narrator
p9n-quiz.text: Hugh's question seven: Gill Sans, nineteen twenty-eight. Then look up in the tower.
p9n-quiz.say: [dry, unhurried] Hugh's question seven: Gill Sans, nineteen twenty-eight. Then look up in the tower.

p9n-rows.speaker: narrator
p9n-rows.text: Glenys in Perth: one bell stopped dead for forty seconds when the lights went, and came back out of breath.
p9n-rows.say: [dry, unhurried] Glenys in Perth: one bell stopped dead for forty seconds when the lights went, and came back out of breath.

p9n-swap.speaker: narrator
p9n-swap.text: Hugh never came, so they all moved up one.

p9n-text.speaker: narrator
p9n-text.text: Hugh, at five past eight: on my way up, something to say about the board.
